title: Processor
summary: Background work as headless isolates, placed by the balancer: a playground where you set each task's CPU and watch it move between worker pools, and a simulated file processor whose processors share their work through consumer groups.

result.line: On 4 cores at 2.0 GHz, 50 files a second and at most 2 workers, the balancer moves processors whose queue keeps growing into a second pool. On Chromium that's 3 workers against a worker each's 9, at a p95 latency of 83 ms against 39 ms and one pool's 153 ms. On Firefox it gets through 49.5 files a second against one pool's 43.8 and a worker each's 50.1, but its p95 reaches 15.5 s. With faults it gets through 46.3 and 33.4 files a second against one pool's 26.8 and 19.7, on 4 workers against 9. It never packed processors back together after the faults, and 3 of 23 runs with faults lost files, and in each the kernel had given up on processors (on @isoloop/*@0.0.0-next.800569e).
